Glencoe and Fort William: The Highland Hub

Glencoe is Britain's most dramatic landscape and Fort William is the Outdoor Capital of the UK. Together, they form a motorcycling base that's hard to beat — world-class roads in every direction, stunning scenery, and excellent facilities for touring riders. Whether you're passing through on a longer Highland tour or making this your destination, you won't be disappointed.

Glen Coe: The Valley

The A82 through Glen Coe is regularly voted Britain's most scenic road. The valley was carved by glaciers and is flanked by towering peaks — the Three Sisters on the south side and Aonach Eagach ridge on the north. The road flows through the valley with sweeping bends and dramatic viewpoints. The Buachaille Etive Mor at the eastern entrance is one of Scotland's most iconic mountains.

Beyond the A82

Glen Coe is more than just the A82. The single-track road to Glen Etive branches south from the main road and follows the River Etive for 12 miles to a dead-end at the loch head. This road featured as the setting for James Bond's Skyfall and is extraordinarily atmospheric. The B863 over the Ballachulish Bridge to Kinlochleven offers a quieter alternative to the main road with mountain views.

Fort William

Fort William sits at the foot of Ben Nevis (1,345m, Britain's highest mountain) and is the natural base for Lochaber exploration. The town has all facilities — fuel, supermarkets, outdoor shops, accommodation at every price point, and excellent restaurants. The West Highland Museum is worth a visit for its Jacobite collections.

Ride the A82 through Glen Coe at dawn or dusk for the most dramatic experience. The light transforms the valley, and you'll likely have the road to yourself.

Rides from Fort William

  • Road to the Isles (A830) — Fort William to Mallaig via Glenfinnan Viaduct (the Harry Potter bridge). Stunning coastal road
  • Glen Nevis — Dead-end road into the shadow of Ben Nevis. Wild and atmospheric
  • Corran Ferry to Ardnamurchan — Short ferry crossing to the most westerly point of the British mainland
  • A86 to Spean Bridge — Fast road through the Great Glen with mountain views

Accommodation

Fort William has extensive accommodation. The Alexandra Hotel in the town centre is biker-friendly with secure parking. The Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe itself is a legendary walkers' and bikers' pub with bar meals and real ales. For camping, the Red Squirrel Campsite at Glen Coe village is popular with motorcyclists.

Practical Information

Fuel is readily available in Fort William and Ballachulish. The nearest motorcycle dealers are in Inverness (65 miles north). Weather in Glen Coe is notoriously wet — the valley funnels Atlantic weather systems and rainfall is among the highest in Britain. Pack waterproofs and appreciate the valley's moody beauty when the clouds descend. Read our Motorcycle Routes Scotland: Complete Guide 2026 | VisorUp guide for more. Read our Bothies and Wild Shelters for Motorcycle Tourers in Scotland guide for more.
keyTakeaways: The A82 through Glen Coe is regularly voted Britain's most scenic road, flanked by the Three Sisters and the Aonach Eagach ridge.
Fort William sits at the foot of Ben Nevis and offers full facilities, making it an ideal touring base for Lochaber.
Detour up the single-track Glen Etive road (the Skyfall setting) and ride the A830 Road to the Isles to Mallaig via the Glenfinnan Viaduct.
The Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe is a legendary bikers' pub, while the Alexandra Hotel in Fort William offers secure parking.
Glen Coe is among the wettest places in Britain, so pack waterproofs and expect moody, atmospheric conditions.

faq.q: Where should I base myself in the area?
faq.a: Fort William is the natural base, sitting at the foot of Ben Nevis with fuel, supermarkets, outdoor shops and accommodation at every price point. The Alexandra Hotel in the town centre is biker-friendly with secure parking. For something more atmospheric, the Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe itself is a legendary walkers' and bikers' pub with real ales and bar meals.

faq.q: What is the best way to experience Glen Coe?
faq.a: Ride the A82 through the glen at dawn or dusk when the light transforms the valley and you will likely have the road to yourself. The Three Sisters loom on the south side and the Buachaille Etive Mor guards the eastern entrance. For more, branch onto the single-track Glen Etive road, which featured in the Bond film Skyfall.

faq.q: Where can I get fuel and servicing?
faq.a: Fuel is readily available in Fort William and Ballachulish. The nearest motorcycle dealers are in Inverness, roughly 65 miles north, so carry basic tools and a tyre repair kit for the more remote roads around Lochaber.

faq.q: What is the weather like in Glen Coe?
faq.a: Glen Coe is notoriously wet. The valley funnels Atlantic weather systems and rainfall is among the highest in Britain. Pack waterproofs and be ready to appreciate the valley's moody beauty when the clouds descend, which they often do even in summer.

faq.q: What day rides work well from Fort William?
faq.a: The A830 Road to the Isles runs to Mallaig past the Glenfinnan Viaduct, Glen Nevis is a wild dead-end beneath Ben Nevis, and the Corran Ferry gives quick access to the Ardnamurchan peninsula and Britain's most westerly mainland point. The A86 to Spean Bridge is a fast run through the Great Glen.
